name: Cocoa flavanols / dark chocolate
short: Across 35 trials, adverse effects such as gastrointestinal complaints and nausea were reported by 1% on cocoa versus 0.4% of controls. A 3.6-year trial in 21,442 older adults found no safety concerns.
text: In a systematic review of 35 randomised trials of chocolate or cocoa products lasting 2 to 18 weeks, cocoa products were generally highly tolerable; adverse effects, including gastrointestinal complaints and nausea, were reported by 1% of participants in the active cocoa groups and 0.4% of those in the control groups, and the authors said long-term trials were needed to assess potential adverse effects of chronic intake. In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of a cocoa extract supplement (500 mg flavanols/day) in 21,442 older adults followed for a median of 3.6 years, the authors reported no safety concerns. In a controlled trial in healthy adults aged 35 to 55, intakes of up to 2000 mg cocoa flavanols/day for 12 weeks produced no significant changes in blood pressure or platelet function, and adverse events were mild and did not differ significantly between study arms. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
